column1: # The values this mod patches, one per line:
#   FILE<TAB>PROPERTY<TAB>BASE<TAB>OP<TAB>LIMIT<TAB>SCOPE
# FILE is the MBIN path the game uses, relative to the data root.
# PROPERTY is the field to rewrite.
# BASE is the value the game ships today.
# OP is mul (BASE x factor) or div (BASE / factor).
# LIMIT is the upper bound for mul and the lower bound for div, so no value
# can reach zero or run away.
# SCOPE tags the row. A variant asks for scopes with a factor each, so one
# group can be scaled differently from another.
# The render step turns this table into the Lua patch list and into the
# expected values that make verify checks the built EXML against.
# The Atlas Interface keeps the whole capture in one entity, unlike the space
# stations, which split it across a dock node and six location entities. So
# the approach, the landing and the departure all come from
# AtlasStation.Entity.MBIN here.
# The scopes:
#   forces    the steering forces that push a ship toward a dock, and that
#             turn it into alignment on the way
#   approach  the speed of the flight through the gate to the pad
#   capture   how far out the interface takes the ship over. Not offered: a
#             probe that makes the capture happen from ten times as far away,
#             so one flight tells whether this file is read at all when the
#             speed values appear to do nothing
#   descent   the speed the ship drops onto the pad
#   bounce    the spring settle and the bounce when the ship touches down
#   manoeuvre the time the ship spends lining up with the pad
#   takeoff   the speed of the flight out of the gate, and the boost on it
#   climb     the time the ship spends rising off the pad and turning out
#   handoff   the speed the player gets control back at
#   height    the height the ship climbs to before it turns out
#   distance  how far it carries on out before the player takes over
# height and distance are not asked for by any variant. They are here so a
# test build can switch one on by adding the scope to a variant, without the
# table having to change. The same goes for descent, which is a candidate for
# why the fly-in reads slow: the ship drops onto the pad at 5, half the
# station's 10.
# The forces, bounce and manoeuvre values are the shared ones from
# GCAISPACESHIPGLOBALS, because the Atlas Interface has no per-location
# equivalent. They are the same bases, ops and limits as Faster Space Station
# Landing uses, so the two mods agree value for value when they are installed
# at the same factor. At different factors the pak the game loads last wins
# for both, which is why both docs tell the user to pick one factor.
# The manoeuvre is shortened by the same factor as the flight. The alignment
# is a manoeuvre of fixed length, so a faster flight only stays upright if it
# is shortened by the same factor; the station landing mod documents the ship
# arriving mid manoeuvre and landing upside down when it is not.
# Deliberately left alone:
#   ApproachNodeTargetOffset and PlayerAutoLandRange, which set where the
#     capture begins rather than how fast it runs. ApproachRange is in the
#     table, but only for the capture probe above; no shipped variant asks
#     for that scope.
#   RotateToDock, which is a flag
#   DockingRotateSpeed, which belongs to Faster Spaceship Docking Rotation
#     Reloaded and is not in this table at all
#   TakeOffExtraAIHeight and TakeOffProgressForExtraHeight, which are about
#     the height NPC ships get after they leave, not about the player's ship
#   PostTakeOffExtraPlayerHeight, which is already 0 and does nothing
#   TakeOffCost, which is launch thruster fuel and not a speed
#   LandingHeight, which is where the ship settles, not how fast
# The game's own spelling of LandingManuevreTime is missing a "u". Do not
# "fix" it here: the name has to match the data byte for byte, and make
# verify fails on a property that is not in the patch.
